claim: One of the UK’s most famous trees—a 150-year-old sycamore growing in a gap along the Roman-era Hadrian’s Wall—was cut down by vandals in 2023.
label: TRUE
annotatorNote: [AI label: Claude, 2026-10-05 - not yet checked by the human annotator] CPS (15 Jul 2025): the tree, planted in the late 19th century, stood in a natural gap next to Hadrian's Wall and was felled overnight on 27-28 Sept 2023 by Daniel Graham and Adam Carruthers, jailed for criminal damage. Late-19th-century planting makes it about 150 years old; the National Trust's 'more than 120 years' is compatible. Some coverage said 200 years (CNN) - an outlier. The article's 'For those who didn't read or weren't aware,' is dropped.
